_comment: Practice items modelled on the workplace-style assessments many hourly employers use in online applications. Scale: 1 Strongly disagree .. 5 Strongly agree. 'reverse': agreeing signals LESS of the trait. 'pair' links two items that should be answered consistently. This is practice and coaching, not a psychological test.

reliability.label: Reliability
reliability.about: Showing up on time, finishing what you start, being someone others can count on.

integrity.label: Honesty & integrity
integrity.about: Telling the truth, following policy, respecting property and money.

teamwork.label: Teamwork
teamwork.about: Helping coworkers, sharing the load, getting along with different people.

service.label: Customer focus
service.about: Patience and respect with customers, residents or the public.

safety.label: Safety & rules
safety.about: Following procedures and safety rules even when it's slower.

steadiness.label: Staying calm
steadiness.about: Handling stress, criticism and busy shifts without losing your cool.

adaptability.label: Adaptability
adaptability.about: Handling change, new tasks and new schedules.

initiative.label: Initiative
initiative.about: Finding work to do and fixing problems without being told.

items.text: I arrive on time, even for things I don't enjoy.
items.coaching: Employers screen hard for attendance. Only agree strongly if it's true, then back it up in the interview with an example.

items.text: It's okay to miss a shift now and then if something better comes up.
items.coaching: This checks the same thing as 'I arrive on time'. Answers that contradict each other get flagged as inconsistent.

items.text: Taking small things from work, like supplies, is no big deal.
items.coaching: Integrity items are pass/fail for many employers. They're looking for clear disagreement.

items.text: I would tell my supervisor if I made a mistake, even if no one noticed.
items.coaching: Owning mistakes is one of the strongest signals of trustworthiness.

items.text: Everyone bends the rules sometimes, so it's fine if I do too.
items.coaching: Statements with 'everyone does it' test whether you'd follow the crowd over policy.

items.text: I help coworkers finish their tasks when I'm done with mine.
items.coaching: They want people who pitch in. Think of a real time you did this for your STARS answers.

items.text: I prefer to work alone and let others handle their own problems.
items.coaching: Liking independent work is fine, but 'let others handle their own problems' reads as not a team player.

items.text: I stay polite with customers even when they are rude to me.
items.coaching: Customer-facing jobs weigh this heavily. Agree only if you can give an example.

items.text: If a customer is being difficult, it's fair to be short with them.
items.coaching: This mirrors 'I stay polite'. Consistent answers matter more than any single one.

items.text: I follow safety procedures even when it slows me down.
items.coaching: Warehouse, kitchen and construction employers treat safety answers very seriously.

items.text: Skipping a safety step is okay if you're experienced.
items.coaching: Experience never replaces procedure in the employer's eyes. Look for clear disagreement.

items.text: I stay calm when a shift gets busy or stressful.
items.coaching: Pair this with a pressure story from your STARS practice.

items.text: When I'm criticised at work, I usually get angry.
items.coaching: Being able to take feedback is key. If this is something you're working on, practise a calm response with your outreach team.

items.text: I'm comfortable when my schedule or tasks change at the last minute.
items.coaching: Hourly jobs change often. Honest answers here also help you find a job that fits your life.

items.text: I get frustrated when I have to learn a new way of doing things.
items.coaching: Coachability matters. Programs and certifications you've completed are proof you learn new things.

items.text: When I finish my work, I look for something else that needs doing.
items.coaching: Employers love self-starters. This mirrors 'I help coworkers finish their tasks'.

items.text: I usually wait to be told what to do next.
items.coaching: Waiting for direction reads as low initiative. Think about what you actually do on a slow shift.

items.text: I have never been late to anything in my life.
items.coaching: Watch out for 'never' and 'always'. Many assessments include these to spot answers that are too good to be true. An honest 'agree' beats an unrealistic 'strongly agree'.

items.text: I have never broken a rule of any kind.
items.coaching: Nobody has literally never broken any rule. These items check whether you're answering honestly; a moderate answer is the honest one.

items.text: I get along with people from different backgrounds.
items.coaching: Diverse workplaces need people who respect everyone. A real example makes this stronger in interviews.
